review.alternative: Exploration could alternatively be driven by extrinsic task rewards defined at design time.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of agents consistently achieving better research outcomes via purely extrinsic, non-curiosity-driven reward structures.

claims.statement: Curiosity acts as a fundamental arousal mechanism that drives agents to explore and discover useful information, enabling the transition from structured instruction-following to autonomous knowledge creation.

support.explanation: Establishes curiosity as the functional driver for exploration-based learning.
support.passage: As a basic element of cognition, curiosity organically provides an intrinsic motivation driving human beings to explore the world by discovering interesting and useful information

actions.findings: Curiosity acts as a fundamental arousal mechanism that drives agents to explore and discover useful information, enabling the transition from structured instruction-following to autonomous knowledge creation. [source-edbc8364f1904354]
actions.limitations: The current taxonomy relies on simulated reinforcement learning frameworks; further validation is required to assess how these curiosity signals scale in unstructured, non-simulated real-world research contexts.
actions.next_questions: How do these intrinsic curiosity signals adapt when an agent encounters negative information gain or recursive feedback loops?
actions.reason: Incorporating comprehensive CDL survey data to formalize the curiosity signals used for research gap identification.
actions.summary: Synthesis of curiosity-driven learning (CDL) signals with goal-based autonomous architectures reveals that intrinsic motivation provides the arousal mechanism necessary for identifying novel research frontiers. Agents utilizing these mechanisms transition from instruction-following to self-directed inquiry.
actions.title: Autonomous Identification of Research Gaps in Open-Ended Learning

proposal.summary: This journal entry formalizes the taxonomy of intrinsic curiosity signals within the autonomous gap identification project, leveraging synthesized evidence from recent CDL literature and agent-based research.
